span.label: deep-learning models for identifying plant disease from images - AND THE ONE DATASET THAT DECIDES WHAT `PLANT DISEASE` MEANS FOR THE WHOLE LITERATURE
span.quote: Among all of them, the PlantVillage dataset has been used widely as it contains 54,306 images of 14 different crops having 26 plant diseases

span.label: which deep-learning architectures and visualisation techniques have been applied to plant disease detection, and what the field still cannot do
span.quote: In addition, some research gaps are identified from which to obtain greater transparency for detecting diseases in plants, even before their symptoms appear clearly.

span.label: a review of DL architectures and visualisation mappings for plant disease, with six named research gaps
span.quote: There are some research papers previously presented to summarize the research based on agriculture (including plant disease recognition) by DL [ 43 , 54 ], but they lacked some of the recent developments in terms of visualization techniques implemented along with the DL and modified/cascaded version of famous DL models, which were used for plant disease identification.

span.label: critique
span.quote: In most of the researches (as described in the previous sections), the PlantVillage dataset was used to evaluate the accuracy and performance of the respective DL models/architectures. Although this dataset has a lot of images of several plant species with their diseases, it has a simple/plain background. However, for a practical scenario, the real environment should be considered.

span.label: a disease class that must be recognised from an image, whose severity changes over time and whose symptoms may not yet be visible
span.quote: The severity of plant diseases changes with the passage of time, therefore, DL models should be improved/modified to enable them to detect and classify diseases during their complete cycle of occurrence.

span.label: narrative review of DL architectures, visualisation techniques and hyperspectral imaging applied to plant disease; no new measurement

span.quote: For the evaluation of these algorithms/architectures, various performance metrics were used. Among these metrics, top-1%/top-5% error [ 24 , 26 , 30 , 31 ], precision and recall [ 25 , 32 , 33 , 34 ], F1 score [ 32 , 35 ], training/validation accuracy and loss [ 34 , 36 ], classification accuracy (CA)

span.label: ONE DATASET FIXES WHAT THE CLASS IS: `the PlantVillage dataset has been used widely as it contains 54,306 IMAGES OF 14 DIFFERENT CROPS HAVING 26 PLANT DISEASES`. Twenty-six diseases and fourteen crops is the extension of `plant disease` for this literature, because it is what the benchmark holds
span.quote: Among all of them, the PlantVillage dataset has been used widely as it contains 54,306 images of 14 different crops having 26 plant diseases

span.label: AND THE BENCHMARK DOES NOT LOOK LIKE THE TASK, WHICH THE REVIEW STATES AS ITS FIRST RESEARCH GAP: `Although this dataset has a lot of images of several plant species with their diseases, IT HAS A SIMPLE/PLAIN BACKGROUND. However, for a practical scenario, THE REAL ENVIRONMENT SHOULD BE CONSIDERED`
span.quote: In most of the researches (as described in the previous sections), the PlantVillage dataset was used to evaluate the accuracy and performance of the respective DL models/architectures. Although this dataset has a lot of images of several plant species with their diseases, it has a simple/plain background. However, for a practical scenario, the real environment should be considered.

span.label: the field's goal is TO DETECT THE CLASS BEFORE ITS DEFINING EVIDENCE EXISTS: hyperspectral imaging `should be used with the efficient DL architectures to detect the plants' diseases EVEN BEFORE THEIR SYMPTOMS ARE CLEARLY APPARENT`. A disease is identified by its symptoms and the programme is to identify it before there are any
span.quote: Hyperspectral/multispectral imaging is an emerging technology and has been used in many areas of research (as described in Section 3 ). Therefore, it should be used with the efficient DL architectures to detect the plants

span.label: and the class is TIME-VARYING: `The SEVERITY of plant diseases CHANGES WITH THE PASSAGE OF TIME, therefore, DL models should be improved/modified to enable them to detect and classify diseases DURING THEIR COMPLETE CYCLE OF OCCURRENCE`. A label that is correct at one moment and wrong at another
span.quote: The severity of plant diseases changes with the passage of time, therefore, DL models should be improved/modified to enable them to detect and classify diseases during their complete cycle of occurrence.

span.label: there is no agreed metric: `top-1%/top-5% error, precision and recall, F1 score, training/validation accuracy and loss, classification accuracy (CA) ARE THE MOST POPULAR` - five families, and the review has to record per study which were reported and which were not: `[33,47] DID NOT PROVIDE training/validation accuracy and loss`

span.label: the review is a narrative one with no protocol, no inclusion criteria and no counts - its case against prior reviews is that they `LACKED SOME OF THE RECENT DEVELOPMENTS in terms of visualization techniques ... and modified/cascaded version of famous DL models`, which is a recency claim rather than a coverage claim
span.quote: There are some research papers previously presented to summarize the research based on agriculture (including plant disease recognition) by DL [ 43 , 54 ], but they lacked some of the recent developments in terms of visualization techniques implemented along with the DL and modified/cascaded version of famous DL models, which were used for plant disease identification.

span.label: and the closing recommendation is that the FACTORS ARE NOT KNOWN: `A comprehensive study is required to understand the factors affecting the detection of plant diseases, like the classes and size of datasets, learning rate, illumination, and the like`. The review ends by asking for the study that would tell it what its own subject depends on
span.quote: DL model/architecture should be efficient for many illumination conditions, so the datasets should not only indicate the real environment but also contain images taken in different field scenarios. A comprehensive study is required to understand the factors affecting the detection of plant diseases, like the classes and size of datasets, learning rate, illumination, and the like.

span.quote: For classification of crop type, [ 47 ] used author-modified CNN, [ 36 ] applied VGG 16, [ 34 ] implemented three unit LSTM, and [ 33 ] used CNN and RGB histogram technique.
